tasks.notes: Scope: the patch adds a second, unrequested 330-line exam, `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs`, at a path outside FILES (FILES names only `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs` as the Test). It is a near-verbatim duplicate of the graded exam — same rig imports, same legs (a)-(m), same M5-M7 document slices, same STUB_CHECKS/STUB_CHECKS_PENDING/STUB_MERGE_CODE cases, same three green and three red conclusions — and it also touches the global constraint 'No file outside a task's own Files block is edited' (a prose constraint with no Check: behind it, hence minor). Two consequences worth acting on: (1) `tests/test_fleet_suite.py:23` globs `fleet/tests/test_*.mjs`, so this file joins the committed suite that is this task's Acceptance, adding ~20 more boots (~40 forks of stub shell each) of runtime for zero new coverage; (2) the driver never ran it — the Proof names only `test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs`, and node execution was denied in this referee sandbox, so whether the committed suite stays green with it is unverified. Any future change to the merge step now has to be transcribed into two exams, and a fix round told to update the named one will leave the unnamed one red. Remedy: delete `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs`; every leg it pins is already pinned by `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs`, which the exam evidence shows at exit 0 with 30 ok lines.; `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh`, the red path of `merge_pr`: `check_runs_verdict` returns the refusal as the space-joined string `red <name> <conclusion>`, and `merge_pr` splits it with `set -- $verdict`, taking `$2` as the check name and `$3` as the conclusion. Any check run whose `name` contains a space — GitHub's ordinary matrix spelling, e.g. `build (3.12)` — shifts the fields: `$2` becomes `build`, `$3` becomes `(3.12)`, and the log line, `MERGE_NOTE`, and the `done` page's phase text then read `merge: check build concluded (3.12) — leaving <pr> open`. The one artifact that tells the operator why their PR was not merged names a conclusion GitHub never returned. The stub's check name is `test`, so the exam cannot see this. Fix inside this task's FILES: delimit the two fields rather than word-splitting them.; `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh`'s own header is now stale about the file it heads. Line 3 still calls the script 'the sandbox side of a run, from the assignment to the PR', and lines 18-19 still say 'The PR is the human gate; there is no write grant to wait for' — but as of this diff the script runs past the PR, polls the head's check runs and squash-merges a ready PR itself, and the human gate has moved to the ready/draft distinction plus `hold=1`. The three operator documents were all updated to say so (M5-M7); the script's own preamble, which is in this task's FILES, was not. Suggested wording: '... from the assignment to the merged PR' in line 3, and in line 18 'A ready PR is the script's own to finish: it merges once the target's checks are green, unless the assignment carries hold=1; a draft is the human gate.'; plan-defect: M4 reads 'Every status page carries a `merged` cell, null on every page before the merge', and this diff duly changed CONTRACT.md's status.json literal to declare `merged` between `prAuthor` and `branch`. But the boot script is not the only writer of a status page: `fleet/setup-script.mjs:86` prints `{"run":…,"state":…,"phase":…,"pr":null,"prAuthor":null,"branch":…,"vm":"","startedAt":…,"updatedAt":…,"error":null}` for the provisioning/pre-boot page, with no `merged` cell — so after this diff the contract literal no longer describes that page. That file is in neither this task's FILES nor any sibling's, so no edit inside this tree answers it; the exam's leg (k) only reaches the boot script's own pages and passes. Nothing consumes the key today (the janitor reads the evidence-branch pages, which the boot script writes), so this blocks nothing — but the operator should decide whether the setup script's page gains the cell in a follow-up or whether CONTRACT.md should say the cell appears from `booting` onward.; Scope: the patch adds a second, near-identical exam at `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs`, a path outside this task's FILES (FILES names exactly one Test: `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs`, and the global constraint says no file outside a task's own Files block is edited). It pins the same clauses M1–M7 and the same legs (a)–(m) as the graded exam, with the same STUB_CHECKS/STUB_CHECKS_PENDING/STUB_MERGE_CODE cases — copy-pasted coverage, two files that must now be kept in lockstep. It also matters for merging: `tests/test_fleet_suite.py:23` globs every `fleet/tests/test_*.mjs`, so the committed suite (this task's Acceptance) will run this file, and it appears in no RUN: or EXAM evidence — ~20 more full boots of stub shell under the suite's 120 s per-file timeout, never observed to pass here. `unverified:` running `node fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs` would settle whether it is green; deleting it settles the scope question and the duplication at once. The graded exam `test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs` covers every leg on its own (EXAM EVIDENCE, exit 0, 30 assertions), so nothing is lost by removing the duplicate.; `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh`, `merge_pr`'s `red*)` arm: `check_runs_verdict` packs the refusal into one space-joined line (`printf 'red %s %s\n' "$name" "$conclusion"`) and the caller unpacks it with `set -- $verdict`, taking `$2` as the check name and `$3` as the conclusion. GitHub check-run names routinely carry spaces (`build (ubuntu-latest)`, `Docs / lint`), and then `$3` is a fragment of the name rather than the conclusion, so the one diagnostic line the operator gets for a refused merge — `merge: check <name> concluded <conclusion> — leaving <pr> open`, and the same text on the `done` page's MERGE_NOTE — names the wrong thing. The unquoted `$verdict` is also subject to pathname expansion, so a name containing `*` or `?` is globbed against the CWD before it is split. The sims only ever use single-word names (`test`, `one`, `two`), so the exam cannot see this. Fix with parameter expansion instead of word splitting, which needs no change to `check_runs_verdict`.; unverified: cross-task claim. `fleet/RUNBOOK.md` ("The PR." paragraph and `## Trust`) and `skills/ultrapowers/SKILL.md` step 4 now tell the operator that `--hold` on the launch line keeps the PR open, but `--hold` is added to `fleet/launch.mjs`'s flag list and USAGE by sibling task 2, whose files this task may not touch. In this task's clone alone the documented flag does not exist, so a reader following the RUNBOOK today would get an unknown-flag refusal. This is the plan's deliberate split (task 2's M1 pins `[--hold]` in USAGE and `hold` in COMMENT_KEYS), and the structural pin the Proof runs — `tests/test_docs_agree_with_code.py`, exit 0 — passes because the sentence is prose rather than part of the documented launch line, so nothing here blocks. What would settle it is the merged tree: `node fleet/tests/test_launch_hold.mjs` and `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_docs_agree_with_code.py` after both tasks fold.; concern: out-of-FILES: fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs — my own exam. The equivalent command I ran clean is `node fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs`.; concern: `--hold` (the launch-line flag that produces `hold=1` in the assignment) is sibling task 2's work in fleet/launch.mjs. fleet/doctor.mjs: `fleetConfigKeys` duplicates `loadFleetConfig`'s read-and-parse body almost line for line (same `fsp.readFile(target,'utf8')` in a bare try/catch, same `JSON.parse` in a second bare try/catch, same `configPath ?? DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH()` resolution) — the only differences are the array rejection and what each returns on failure. `main` then reads the same path twice, once per function, so a file rewritten between the two calls yields a `config` and a `configKeys` that describe different file contents. Both would collapse onto one private helper, e.g. `async function readConfigObject (target) { try { const parsed = JSON.parse(await fsp.readFile(target, 'utf8')); return (parsed && typeof parsed === 'object' && !Array.isArray(parsed)) ? parsed : null } catch { return null } }`, with `loadFleetConfig` folding its two keys over the defaults from it and `fleetConfigKeys` answering `Object.keys(...)`. Not blocking: the behaviour the exam grades is correct as written, and `loadFleetConfig`'s current array handling (line 133 accepts an array and finds no string keys on it) is BASE's, untouched by this diff.; skills/ultrapowers/SKILL.md and skills/ultrapowers/references/first-run.md are in this task's own Files block *and* in the Files blocks of concurrent siblings (SKILL.md in tasks 1, 2 and 3; first-run.md in task 3), so this is authorized, not a scope escape — the plan put four concurrent tasks in one wave over the same two documents. Recording it only so the operator knows the textual merge is expected: this diff's hunks are the `## Setup` capacity paragraph in SKILL.md (context lines `Then the agent asks, again with AskUserQuestion` / `AskUserQuestion: **Lower the run size, or upgrade the plan?**`) and the `## capacity` section of first-run.md, neither of which is the region tasks 1–3 rewrite (SKILL.md steps 2, 4 and 5; first-run.md's exe-dev bullet at line ~39). No action required unless the wave's merge reports a conflict there.

completenessFindings.detail: fleet/RUNBOOK.md:28 (Task 1, Claim/M6 — RUNBOOK.md is in Task 1's Files block): the document's opening overview still ends the run's story at "opens the PR over GitHub's REST API through the edge. The PR is the human gate; there is no approval step before it." After Task 1 that is no longer true for a ready PR, and the same document now says the opposite twice — line 173 ("A ready PR merges itself: the sandbox polls its head's check runs and squash-merges it once every check is green") and line 400 ("a pull request whose merge waits on the target's own checks, and --hold to keep a human at the merge button"). Task 1's M6 named only the "The PR." paragraph, the States table's done row and the Trust section, all three of which are correct; the overview paragraph was in scope (same file, same task) and was left stale, so an operator reading the RUNBOOK top-down is told the PR is a human gate and then, 145 lines later, that it merges itself.

fleet/CONTRACT.md:193-194 vs fleet/doctor.mjs:253-266 and skills/ultrapowers/references/first-run.md:75-77 (Task 4, Claim): the contract's "Laptop config ~/.ultrapowers/fleet.json" bullet still reads "exactly two keys, both optional, an unknown key ignored and a missing file meaning the defaults". After Task 4 an unknown key is not ignored — capacityRow returns a `missing` (red) capacity row naming it, and the CLI exits 1 — and first-run.md was updated to say exactly that ("a key the doctor does not read is named in the red detail, and the agent rewrites the file with cpu and memory only"). Two of the four operator documents now describe the same file format in contradictory terms. Note this was not fixable inside the run as planned: CONTRACT.md is not in Task 4's Files block, and the global constraint forbids editing a file outside it — the gap is in the plan's scoping, not in the delivered code, which is why this is minor rather than blocking.
